note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain following a skiing injury sustained on Sunday, approximately 4 days ago. While skiing and attempting moguls, the patient's ski strap became caught on her finger, causing it to hyperextend or bend backward. The patient reports the pain is exacerbated with movement. She has attempted conservative management with ice application and ibuprofen, but continues to experience significant pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reviewed and unremarkable except for chief complaint.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation (recent)
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, patient self-administered)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger examined. Tenderness elicited over the distal phalanx and distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Patient able to flex, extend, and touch thumb to finger with pain on flexion noted.

RESULTS
X-rays of right index finger: Normal with no fractures identified. Good alignment of bone structures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger contusion (distal phalanx). No fracture. Patient to be fitted with aluminum foam splint. Prescribed Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately one week. Patient advised to call and return for follow-up evaluation if symptoms do not improve.
